title: Gandhi and King
hook: a Baptist pastor credits a Hindu lawyer with his method. how?
tomorrow: why would King call his trip to India a pilgrimage?

segments.voice: Yesterday in Gandhi and King: a war poem read as the war inside, and the work done without grabbing at its fruit. Today, the same idea turns up somewhere nobody expected.
screen: `THE FRUIT WAS NEVER YOURS TO HOLD.`

segments.voice: Plenty of people pick up something that lasts from someone of another faith: a coach, a neighbor, a teacher at the gym. Martin Luther King Jr. did it in front of the whole country, and he left behind an odd sentence about it. A Baptist pastor, writing about the movement he led, gives the credit to two people. Christ, he says, gave the spirit and the motivation. Gandhi, a Hindu lawyer from the other side of the world, gave the method. So how does a Baptist pastor end up with a Hindu's method? He tells the story himself.
screen: `SOMETHING LEARNED ACROSS FAITHS.` → `CHRIST THE SPIRIT, GANDHI THE METHOD.` → `HOW DOES THAT HAPPEN?`

segments.voice: In Stride Toward Freedom, his book about the Montgomery bus boycott, King says that as a seminary student in Pennsylvania he had nearly decided that love works between two people and fails against a whole unjust system. Then he heard a sermon about Gandhi, and it moved him so much that he went out and bought books on Gandhi's life and work. In them he saw love lifted into a force that could move a whole community, without hatred and without weapons. That's the first half of the puzzle. The second half is what he didn't do. King stayed a Christian minister. He didn't become a Hindu. What crossed the ocean was satyagraha and ahimsa, a Hindu man's way of holding truth without harm, taken up by a Baptist pastor to live out his own faith. King lists the marks of this nonviolence. It resists; it isn't for cowards. It tries to win the opponent's friendship, not to humiliate them. It aims at the wrong, not at the people caught in it. And it accepts suffering without hitting back. So the puzzle solves itself. A method can travel. The faith underneath it doesn't have to be traded in for it. Both stayed themselves, and they met in one movement.
screen: `LOVE AGAINST A WHOLE SYSTEM?` · `A SERMON, THEN A STACK OF BOOKS.` · `HE STAYED A CHRISTIAN MINISTER.` · `THE METHOD CROSSED THE OCEAN.` · then, large: `A METHOD CAN TRAVEL.`

segments.voice: Count, on your fingers, the people from a background different from yours who taught you something you still use: a recipe, a habit, a way of saying sorry. Give each one a slow breath and a silent thank-you. If the count runs past your fingers, start again on the first.
Gandhi and King: today, a pastor's faith and a Hindu's method, meeting in one movement without either giving way.
Your line from Gandhi and King: the spirit can come from one place and the method from another. See you tomorrow.
